name: workflow + diagram decisions (ADR index)
description: Agentic context model + living drawio diagram + this workflow (ADR-0014, ADR-0015, ADR-0016). The diagram is a source of truth — update it in the same change as any system-shape change.

content: When recording index/reference mulch records, pass --files explicitly — ml auto-fills files[] from the ENTIRE working-tree changeset when omitted, polluting the record. Also: treehouse.toml post_create must be a TOML array (post_create = ["pnpm install"]); mulch reference records require --name; sd plan step priority must be an integer and 'alternatives' section wants objects not strings.

name: deep-module design tenet (ADR index)
description: Design deep modules: a small interface over a large implementation, at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Vocabulary (module/interface/depth/seam/adapter) + module-depth as a review criterion; operative checklist in docs/conventions.md. Open ADR-0017 before changing.

sd plan submit rejects an 'alternatives' section written as a list of strings — 'sd plan prompt' labels it '(list)' but each item must be an object {name, rejected_because}. Plain strings fail validation with 'sections.alternatives.N must be a object'.
resolution: Author alternatives as objects: [{"name":"...","rejected_because":"..."}]. risks/acceptance remain plain-string lists; only alternatives is object-shaped.

name: same-tree parallel subagents for disjoint doc edits
description: In a /feature Phase-2 wave where the ready seeds edit STRICTLY DISJOINT files and perform NO git/sd/ml ops, fan out same-session subagents in the shared working tree instead of cold treehouse worktrees. The orchestrator holds all VCS/seeds/mulch bookkeeping (claim/close/commit) at the barrier; subagents only edit their owned files and return a structured summary. Cheaper than worktrees for docs-only multi-file changes; treehouse isolation is still required when agents touch overlapping files or run their own gate/push.

content: The living drawio diagram (ADR-0015) shows external-service state through node STYLE: dashed-grey (fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#999999;dashed=1;fontColor=#666666) = deferred/stubbed; solid-orange (fillColor=#ffe6cc;strokeColor=#d79b00) = live/active. When a service goes live (ADR-0018: e_resend mail deferred→live; e_gateway now 'Gateway (default) OR direct Anthropic/Voyage by key'), flip BOTH the label AND the style, keep the a_adr node's ADR range current (now 0001–0018), then regenerate deliverables: drawio -x -f svg -e -o resonance-architecture.svg ... and -f png -o resonance-architecture.drawio.png. Validate XML first. drawio CLI is at /opt/homebrew/bin/drawio.

description: no-mistakes (v1.31.2) can't gate treehouse-worktree branches: 'no previous run for branch' — runs bind to the MAIN working copy's branch.
resolution: This run: crewmates fell back to local scoped turbo gates + manual PRs; orchestrator ran the integrated turbo gate centrally (31/31); compensate the missing review leg with /code-review on the integrated diff or CI. Future runs: (1) upgrade no-mistakes to v1.34.0; (2) restructure the feature loop so crewmates run only the fast local gate in-worktree and the ORCHESTRATOR runs the full no-mistakes gate (incl. code-review) on the integrated branch in the main checkout at each barrier. Tracked by resonance-3e21.

name: Design fidelity via the visual manifest
description: Verify UI against Figma using design/manifest/ (per screen: design.png contract + design.md spec + app.png). GOLDEN RULE: the Figma frame is the definitive source of truth — match pixel-for-pixel, drive drift to zero, read the frame, never assume. Patterns (conversation-first, no cards) are a LENS not a rule; defer to the frame per screen incl. exceptions. CODIFIED (resonance-042f, was 'tracked'): ratified as ADR-0019 (R1 verified provenance, R2 artifact-anchored parity 'matches design.png except [deltas]', R3 provisional stays visible, R4 Code Connect); add-ui-component-from-figma recipe is now verify-MANDATORY (Step 8 = capture + pixel-diff); a project verify skill (.claude/skills/verify) carries the UI pixel-diff branch; capture generalized to apps/web/scripts/capture-route.mjs <route> <out> (+ shared lib/harness-session.mjs) alongside capture-app-manifest.mjs; golden rule added to root CLAUDE.md (rule 10). Loop: change code, re-capture under E2E_HARNESS=1, pixel-sample bytes with sharp vs design.png (perception lies).

Figma MCP is billed PER TEAM not per user: a file in a Starter-tier team hits a low daily cap even if you hold Pro on a different team (whoami lists your teams and tiers). After the cap trips or an MCP reconnect, get_screenshot and get_metadata can silently drop (return tool not found) while get_design_context and download_assets keep working.
resolution: Move the design file into the Pro-tier team (same file key; Figma preserves node ids across the move). Use download_assets for renders (short-lived savable URLs, tolerates parallel calls) and get_design_context for specs plus an inline screenshot. Reconnect the MCP after moving. Fix the stale packages/ui/CLAUDE.md note claiming the team copy has a higher MCP budget.

description: no-mistakes axi run / rerun fail with 'no previous run for branch <b>' on a fresh branch — the axi interface does NOT create the first run; only a push to the 'no-mistakes' git-remote proxy (which fires a receive/notify-push hook) creates it. Updating v1.31.2->v1.40.3 and 'daemon restart' did NOT fix it (that was the resonance-3e21 hypothesis).
resolution: Trigger the first run via the git remote: if 'git push no-mistakes <branch>' says 'Everything up-to-date' (ref already mirrored, hook never fired), force it with 'git push no-mistakes :<branch>' then 'git push no-mistakes <branch>'. The re-push fires notify-push and the daemon creates the run even if the push prints a socket i/o-timeout on the notify ack. Then drive/attach with 'no-mistakes axi run --intent ...' (HEAD matches). The gate also auto-fixes pre-existing CI failures in its ci step and pushes fix commits; 'no-mistakes axi sync' fast-forwards local to the pipeline head afterward.

description: In a treehouse worktree, 'sd create' writes to the MAIN repo's .seeds/issues.jsonl (seeds resolves the tracker to the main checkout, like mulch does with .mulch/), NOT to the worktree's tracked copy. The new seed is therefore invisible on the feature branch: 'sd show <id>' succeeds from inside the worktree, but the branch's own .seeds/issues.jsonl is a stale snapshot from branch-creation time. This produced a false-positive no-mistakes 'document' gate finding - a doc citing a freshly filed follow-up seed was flagged as a broken anchor because the reviewer resolved the id against the worktree's .seeds/ and did not find it.
resolution: Verify with 'grep -rln <id> <main-repo>/.seeds/' before believing the gate: if the id is in the main repo's issues.jsonl, the seed is real and the finding is a visibility artifact of the worktree, so approve the gate and let the tracker state land on main via the orchestrator's 'sd sync'. Do NOT copy the main repo's issues.jsonl into the feature branch to satisfy the check - it drags every concurrent crewmate's tracker edits onto the branch and guarantees merge conflicts. When a crewmate needs to cite a follow-up seed in a docstring, create the seed FIRST and confirm the returned id, never invent one - and expect the citation to be unverifiable from inside the worktree.

description: ADR-0019's documented Figma capture path is dead: FIGMA_ACCESS_TOKEN returns 403, so every REST-backed tool fails — figma_get_file_data, figma_get_file_versions, figma_get_file_at_version, download_assets, get_screenshot, get_metadata. design/manifest/README.md documented download_assets as THE procedure, which is a trap for the next agent. A second consequence is that Figma version ids are unobtainable, so captures cannot be version-pinned.
resolution: Capture through the Desktop Bridge plugin instead (mcp__figma-console__figma_execute + figma_capture_screenshot). To get PNG bytes onto disk: run a local HTTP receiver on a port in 9223-9232 (the bridge plugin's networkAccess.allowedDomains only permits http://localhost on those ports; use hostname 'localhost', NOT 127.0.0.1), then from figma_execute do node.exportAsync({format:'PNG',constraint:{type:'SCALE',value:1}}) -> figma.base64Encode(bytes) -> fetch POST to the receiver. Batch several frames per figma_execute call. Substitute a SHA-256 of design.png for the missing version id: exportAsync at a fixed scale is byte-reproducible, so an unchanged frame re-exports to an identical hash (verified). Full procedure now in design/manifest/README.md § Capture notes.

description: The figma-console Desktop Bridge (v1.37.1 server / v1.35.0 plugin) drops its websocket constantly during a read session. A successful figma_execute is frequently followed by 'Unable to establish connection to Figma after 10 seconds' or 'Connection replaced by same file reconnection' on the very next call. It is not the code and not a real failure. Separately, getNodeByIdAsync HANGS (times out, then kills the connection) on instance-internal ids of the form I<instance>;<child> — the ones the bridge itself reports when you walk a tree. Also documentAccess is 'dynamic-page', so synchronous accessors like node.mainComponent throw and you must use getMainComponentAsync/getNodeByIdAsync/loadAllPagesAsync.
resolution: Call figma_reconnect and retry — it recovers immediately. Prefer few large figma_execute calls over many small ones, since each call is a chance to drop. Never pass an I<a>;<b> id to getNodeByIdAsync: resolve the PARENT instance by its plain id and walk its .children array instead. Verify the bridge with figma_diagnose then figma_get_status probe:true at session start, and confirm the reported fileName/fileKey is the file you mean to cite before capturing.

title: Pin design/manifest captures with a SHA-256 of design.png, and flag copy-derived provenance, while Figma REST is 403
rationale: The manifest cites node ids from a COPY of the designer's file (vC0O5uyMmw1o5vYHmCoOXq 'Resonance (Copy)' for screens 08-12; UYlkCL7jkCVgKWiqAVlEFp for 01-07; the designer's canonical file is neither). Figma preserves node ids across a copy, so an id resolves forever while its MEANING drifts as the designer edits the original. The citation never fails — it just quietly stops describing the right frame. That is the exact self-certification failure ADR-0019 exists to prevent, reintroduced one layer down. The natural fix, recording a Figma version id per capture, is impossible because REST is 403. DECISION: record fileKey + nodeId + capturedAt + designPngSha256 + provenance:copy-derived in every design.md, and add design/manifest/PROVENANCE.md stating plainly which file the manifest trusts and what that is worth. The hash works as a drift detector because exportAsync at a fixed scale is byte-reproducible. LIMIT, stated explicitly: content hashing catches drift WITHIN the file we can see, never drift BETWEEN the copy and the canonical file — the copy is frozen, so its hash matches happily while the real design moves. Only migrating to read-only access on the canonical file fixes that, filed as resonance-6db8 with an ADR-0019 amendment. Corollary: this workflow only ever READS Figma, so a copy buys nothing and costs integrity for free — never call a Figma write tool against a design file.

description: Seeds/mulch tracker state is git-tracked in .seeds/*.jsonl and .mulch/*.jsonl, so it is BRANCH-SCOPED. During a /feature fan-out the orchestrator submitted a plan (pl-bbca) and closed seeds while on the slice branch feat/member-discovery-core, then checked out main after merging two subagent PRs. On main the plan and all six child seeds did not exist, 'sd ready' returned a stale list, and an already-closed seed (resonance-c2d2) reappeared as open. Compounding it: subagent 'sd close' / 'sd create' calls made inside a treehouse worktree write to the MAIN repo's .seeds/, i.e. whatever branch the orchestrator has checked out - so tracker mutations from PR work never appear in that PR's diff (verified: PRs #8 and #9 touched zero .seeds/.mulch files).
resolution: Orchestrator must stay on ONE branch for the whole fan-out and never check out another branch while subagents are running, because their tracker writes target the orchestrator's working tree. Keep the slice branch rebased onto origin/main as subagent PRs merge (git rebase origin/main) rather than switching to main - that keeps merged code and tracker state on one history. Diagnose with: git branch --contains <plan-commit> and 'grep -c pl-<id> .seeds/plans.jsonl' on each branch. Do not run 'sd' commands after switching branches until you have confirmed which branch holds authoritative tracker state.

content: A @resonance/db adapter for a @resonance/core port takes its cross-package collaborators as INJECTED functions, never imports. createDiscoveryAdapter({ db, embed }) needs text->vector but must not import @resonance/ai, because the dependency runs ai -> db (ADR-0003). The app layer wires (text) => resolveEmbedder().embed(text); tests inject a deterministic fake. Same rule that makes Db the first argument of every query helper: accept dependencies, don't create them. Symptom that you got it backwards: db's package.json would need @resonance/ai.

title: Injected cross-package collaborators are stated, not drawn, in the architecture diagram
rationale: Slice A wires @resonance/ai's embed() into @resonance/db's createDiscoveryAdapter from apps/web. Drawing that as an ai->db edge in resonance-architecture.drawio is actively misleading: it reads as a package dependency, which ADR-0003 forbids and which does not exist (db never imports ai). The first attempt drew the edge and it also overlapped both node labels, which is how the problem surfaced. Resolution: express injected collaboration in the packages-tier boundary NOTE ('cross-package collaborators are INJECTED by the app, not imported'), and reserve edges for real dependencies and data flows. Self-checking the regenerated PNG with vision is what caught both the overlap and the semantic error - validate.py reported 0 errors on the misleading version.

description: A vertical slice ran six steps and merged five PRs — all gates green — while the feature was BROKEN in the actual environment. Migration 0003 (follows) was committed to main but never applied to the dev Neon database; because searchCreatorProfiles only emits its follows sub-select when a viewer is present, anonymous /discover worked and every AUTHENTICATED search 500'd. Nothing caught it because typecheck/lint/unit/build/CI never touch a running database, and apps/web/.env.local is gitignored so it never reaches a treehouse worktree — no step before the last could boot the app against real infrastructure even if it wanted to. The orchestrator (and the crewmates) read 'gates green' as 'feature works'.
resolution: Treat 'gates green' and 'verified working' as different claims and report them separately. Concretely: (1) scripts/verify-live.mjs now compares drizzle's journal against drizzle.__drizzle_migrations and names missing tags, so this class of drift is a one-command detection — verified it reports '0003_green_ultimo' against the real pre-fix state; (2) do NOT auto-apply migrations to close the gap — drizzle-kit renders a rename as DROP COLUMN + ADD COLUMN, so unattended application is silent data loss; detection plus an explicit 'committed, NOT applied' handoff is the safe shape; (3) order the DAG so something RUNS early — a slice that only becomes runnable at the final step defers all integration risk to the end; (4) worktree credentials are tracked by resonance-8aff (per-worktree Neon branch + sink email, not a copy of the real .env.local, because up to max_trees=16 agents would otherwise hold live write access).

name: Weave OS architecture (ADR index)
description: Weave OS: corpus is repo-versioned YAML in @resonance/weave-os compiled at build (no runtime fs reads); resolveWeaveOs is the seam and returns {system,flow,outputs,releaseId}; governance is git plus CODEOWNERS + evolution_policy enforcement (spec sections 16/17 NOT built); Pattern Registry splits rulebook-YAML / records-Postgres; inheritance normalized child-side. Also ratifies the request-scoped runner (ADR-0009) vs job-scoped executor boundary — the executor is deliberately undesigned. Open ADR-0020 before changing.

Branching off a non-main feature branch inherits its CI breaks: feat/weave-os-foundation added five Weave design docs that are verbatim Google Docs exports, and they fail 'pnpm format:check' (a CI step) on that branch. Every crewmate branching from it would have shipped a red PR for a break it did not cause, and 'prettier --write' would have corrupted the escaped characters the corpus transcription reads from.
resolution: Verify a base-branch break is pre-existing before owning it (git stash -u; git checkout <base>; run the gate; checkout back). Fix by ignoring, not reformatting: added docs/Weave*.md and 'docs/Emerging Creator Onboarding Interview Flow.md' to .prettierignore, matching the existing 'do not hand-format' entries for drizzle and .mulch.

title: Transcribed corpus content ships with its defects named, not repaired
rationale: Three designer documents were transcribed into packages/weave-os/corpus. Where a source does not determine an answer the transcription carries what was written, adds a numbered entry to packages/weave-os/DEFECTS.md, and stops. The load-bearing case: the interview flow's applied_principles names seven principle ids the principles file does not define, and the cross-file validator ships FAILING on all seven by name, pinned by a test. Mapping them to nearest, inventing the missing principles, or downgrading the field to free-form tags would each author the designer's semantics on their behalf — the exact drift the corpus's source+confidence provenance exists to prevent. A named, tested failure is cheaper than a plausible-looking guess nobody can later distinguish from the author's intent.

name: authored YAML compiled to a committed TS module
description: A package that hosts authored data (the Weave OS corpus) keeps YAML as the authoring format and commits a GENERATED TypeScript module beside it, so nothing reads the filesystem at runtime. The shape: corpus/*.yaml -> scripts/compile-corpus.ts (the ONLY fs reader) -> src/corpus.generated.ts holding a deepFreeze'd literal. Three details make it hold. (1) The codegen emits deepFreeze<T>(...) with an explicit type argument: without it TS infers a union over the heterogeneous array and synthesises optional-undefined members that fail the open Record types. (2) The generated file goes in .prettierignore, because a --check mode compares it byte-for-byte and reformatting would report drift that does not exist. (3) YAML is parsed with js-yaml's JSON_SCHEMA, not its default, so 2026-07-14 stays a string and 'no' stays a word. corpus:check runs as the first half of build AND a test asserts the same equality, so the fast gate catches an uncompiled edit too.

'ml add <domain>' and 'ml record' inside a treehouse worktree write to the MAIN repo's .mulch/ (mulch resolves .mulch/ to the main checkout so expertise survives worktree cleanup). The worktree branch therefore does NOT get .mulch/expertise/<domain>.jsonl, and 'pnpm check:workspace' — which runs 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' from cwd, i.e. the worktree — fails CI with 'no mulch domain <name>' even though 'ml status' shows the domain present.
resolution: After recording, copy the two files from the main checkout into the worktree and commit them on the branch: cp <main>/.mulch/mulch.config.yaml .mulch/ && cp <main>/.mulch/expertise/<domain>.jsonl .mulch/expertise/. Then re-run 'node scripts/check-workspace-integrity.mjs'. Leave the main checkout's copy alone — reverting it would clobber a concurrent crewmate's domain addition, and the content is identical so git merges it trivially.

title: Weave OS / Evolution Engine build deferred until explicit notice
rationale: The blocker is the source design, not engineering. Two of four root files (weave_behavior_rules, weave_conversation_heuristics) and five of six active flows were never authored; there are two incompatible principle vocabularies and two incompatible stage vocabularies; and inheritance is declared in both directions, so a promotion into either promotion-target file reaches no conversation. 25 defects in packages/weave-os/DEFECTS.md (4 blocking) require the designer. Meanwhile ~11,769 lines of governance machinery had landed to govern 49 lines of prompt with nothing wired, so pausing costs nothing and continuing would compound interpretation risk.

description: Reporting 'the gate is running' after launching 'no-mistakes axi run' is unfounded, and was wrong twice in one session. Two distinct causes. (1) TOOL SHAPE: axi run prints failures to STDOUT as 'error: ...' and still EXITS 0 (its documented codes are 0 for success/no-op/decision-gates), so a run that never started looks identical to a healthy one — especially when backgrounded, where the error text is in a file nobody read. A real instance: axi run died with 'push rejected (non-fast-forward)' against the gate bare repo and created no run at all, yet exit 0 plus backgrounding was reported to the user as 'the gate is running'. (2) NARRATION AS ACTION: ending a turn on 'I'll pick up <seed> now' without calling anything leaves nothing running, while reading to the user as though work had started.
resolution: Never infer a gate run from the launch command. After starting one, VERIFY with 'no-mistakes axi status' and require BOTH: a run whose status is non-terminal (running / awaiting_approval, not cancelled|failed|passed|checks-passed), AND run.head equal to 'git rev-parse --short HEAD'. A head mismatch means you are looking at a stale run, which is how a cancelled run gets misread as live. Only after that check may you tell the user it is gating. Corollary for any backgrounded command whose tool prints errors to stdout: exit 0 is not evidence — grep the output file for '^error:' before reporting. And never end a turn on a stated intention: either make the call in that turn, or say explicitly that it has not been started yet.

description: A second custody-divergence shape in the no-mistakes gate, distinct from the one seed resonance-dcb6 records. In dcb6 the gate's rebase wrote objects into the bare repo but NEVER advanced the branch ref. Here the opposite: the gate ref HAD advanced to its own rebased copy of the branch (new SHAs on top of a freshly merged main), while the local branch had resolved the same conflict with a MERGE commit. Neither ref was an ancestor of the other, so 'git push no-mistakes <branch>' and every 'axi run' were rejected non-fast-forward, while 'axi status' unhelpfully reported next_action code 'run_pipeline'. Updating v1.40.3 to v1.41.2 did NOT fix it — the update only cleared a daemon-level refusal to update while a stale run was registered; the divergence is a plain git fact, not a tool bug. The gate's rebased tree was ALSO not a valid substitute for the local one: it was missing a later follow-up commit (a parity-doc note) the local branch had.
resolution: Do not reset, force-push, or edit the gate's internal repo. Record a 'git merge -s ours <gate-remote>/<branch>' into the LOCAL branch: that makes HEAD a descendant of the gate ref so the push becomes a legal fast-forward, while keeping the local tree byte-identical and dropping no commit from either side. PROVE the tree is untouched rather than assuming — capture 'git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}' before and after and assert equality. Then push, and re-verify the run actually started. Prerequisite: a stale run registered as active will block 'no-mistakes update' — 'axi abort --run <id>' it first (safe once it already refuses 'axi respond', which means it is terminal in practice).

description: Watching a no-mistakes run for completion with 'until axi status | grep -qE "awaiting_approval|^outcome:"' NEVER fires on a successful run. The ci step deliberately stays status=running after checks pass, monitoring the PR until it is merged or closed, so a healthy finished run reports 'status: running' with ci,running for hours and prints no 'outcome:' line in axi status. The terminal 'outcome: checks-passed' appears only in the ORIGINAL axi run/respond command's stdout, not in later status queries. Combined with the earlier exit-code trap this made three separate 'I'll report when it lands' promises silently never arrive.
resolution: Do not poll axi status for a completion word. Detect a finished run by STEP STATE instead: the run is done when steps push and pr are 'completed' and ci is either completed or running-with-'all CI checks passed' in its last_activity. Concretely: 'no-mistakes axi status | grep -E "^    (push|pr),completed"' plus checking the ci activity line, or simply query the PR: 'gh pr checks <n>' / 'gh pr view <n> --json mergeable'. Corollary on exit codes for this tool: they carry NO information about run state in EITHER direction — exit 0 has hidden a run that never started (push rejected), and exit 1 has hidden a run that was healthy and mid-fix (client stream disconnect while the daemon kept working). Only step state answers the question.

description: Backticks inside a double-quoted shell argument are COMMAND SUBSTITUTION, so any ml record description or no-mistakes --intent that quotes code with backticks silently loses that text. Hit twice in one session: a crewmate had its whole --intent evaluate to empty (the gate then reviewed with no context and logged "no matching agent transcript found"), and an ml record description lost the word it was quoting, leaving the stored text reading "omits  so the port ranks" with a shell error printed alongside a SUCCESS message. The write succeeds, so nothing fails loudly and the corruption is only visible by reading the record back.
resolution: Never put backticks in a double-quoted --description or --intent. Use SINGLE quotes for the whole argument, or drop the backticks and name the thing in prose or caps. For long intents, write the text to a file and pass "$(cat file)" so quoting is handled once. ALWAYS read the record back after writing one that quotes code: ml search <name> and grep for a distinctive phrase, because ml prints a success tick even when the shell ate part of the input.

description: The no-mistakes gate can never run a browser E2E in this repo, and will raise it as a finding on every such change. It validates committed history in an isolated clone, and DATABASE_URL lives only in gitignored apps/web/.env.local, so the app cannot boot there. Its fallbacks are closed too, one of them circularly: the Neon MCP server is configured as npx server-postgres with DATABASE_URL interpolated, so it cannot start without the variable it would have provided access to. There is no env-passthrough flag on axi run or in the config.
resolution: Expect the finding and decide it once: the browser evidence comes from CI, which injects DATABASE_URL from repo secrets, plus a local run by the author. Do not re-ask the user the same structural finding on a later run of the same branch. The durable fix is per-run ephemeral Neon branches for CI E2E, which would also make cross-run fixture pollution structurally impossible.

description: sd plan edit --step N --title propagates the new title to the WRONG child seed - it landed step 4's title on the step-3 child (resonance-0084, the db step), silently overwriting it with the web step's title while the seed kept its own db label. Two separate edits also printed no propagation line at all, so the misfire is invisible unless you re-read every child. Tracker state looked plausible - a real title on a real seed - which is exactly why it survives a glance; the label/title mismatch was the only tell.
resolution: After any sd plan edit --step, re-read EVERY child title (loop sd show over the child ids and print the title line) and compare against the plan's steps. Do not trust the propagation line, including its absence. Repair with sd update <seed> --title directly, which targets one seed and cannot misfire.

description: The tracker files are marked merge=union in .gitattributes (.seeds/issues.jsonl, .seeds/plans.jsonl, .mulch/expertise/*.jsonl). Union appends both sides rather than conflicting, which is correct when two branches touch DIFFERENT seeds but silently corrupts the file when both touch the SAME seed: the merged file then holds two lines sharing one id, with different statuses. It also produces a confusing symptom - git merge-tree locally reports a CLEAN merge because it applies the union driver, while GitHub reports the PR as CONFLICTING because it does not apply merge drivers when computing mergeability. Hit on PR #27: main carried resonance-abbc as in_progress, the feature branch carried the older open line, and the union merge kept both.
resolution: After any rebase or merge that touches .seeds or .mulch, scan for duplicate ids before committing - parse the jsonl and count ids, do not trust a clean merge exit code. Resolve by keeping the entry with the newest updatedAt and dropping the rest, then run sd doctor. Note sd doctor reports bidirectional blocks/blockedBy mismatches as a WARNING and main already carries about 103 of them, so a rising count there is not necessarily caused by your change - compare against origin/main before chasing it.
